classification.difficultyReason: Student identifies the compound graph and gives a reason, reads a value off the graph, does a three-year compound table, and finds a difference. All steps are routine and signposted.

content.prompt: $\$4000$ is invested for 4 years at 10% p.a. Option A pays simple interest and Option B pays compound interest, compounded annually. The graph shows the value of each option.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Which option is compound interest? Give a reason.

answer.short: Option B. Its graph is a curve that gets steeper, while Option A is a straight line.
answer.worked: Simple interest adds the same amount each year, so its graph is a straight line (Option A). Compound interest adds more each year because interest is earned on previous interest, so its graph curves upward (Option B).

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use the graph to find the value of Option A at the end of year 3.

answer.worked: Read the value of the straight line at year 3: $\$5200$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the value of Option B at the end of year 3 by calculating the interest earned each year.

children.label: d
children.prompt: How much more is Option B worth than Option A at the end of year 3?
